sectorNotes.wildlife: Rotor sweep and tower lighting raise collision risk for bats on Sint-Pietersberg and for commuting raptors.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Small concrete pad and crane hardstand; limited soil sealing compared with other types.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: No process discharge. Spill risk is limited to maintenance oils on the pad.
sectorNotes.energy: High local renewable yield; one turbine covers several hundred households in a windy year.
sectorNotes.jobs: Short construction peak plus a handful of ongoing service visits.
sectorNotes.carbon: Avoids grid gas generation once built; payback is a few months of operation.
sectorNotes.society: Close neighbours get flicker and a moving silhouette on the skyline.
sectorNotes.noise: Broadband swish is strongest within a few hundred metres, especially downwind at night.

sectorNotes.wildlife: Fenced grassland is lost to ground-nesting birds; some insects use panel shade later.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Pile foundations and access tracks seal and compact soil across the array.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: Panels themselves are inert; silt from grading can reach ditches during build.
sectorNotes.energy: Steady daytime output that pairs well with city demand, weaker in December.
sectorNotes.jobs: Install crews for a season, then occasional cleaning and electrical checks.
sectorNotes.carbon: Displaces fossil peakers on bright weekdays; manufacturing debt is paid within years.
sectorNotes.society: Low profile after planting; glare complaints are uncommon at this latitude.
sectorNotes.noise: Inverters hum on the pad; inaudible beyond the fence for this layout.

sectorNotes.wildlife: Night lighting, noise, and a hard edge push mammals and birds out of the inner ring.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Yard runoff can carry oils and metals into soil unless the pad is fully bunded.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: Process and wash-water risk is the main water pathway if drains reach the Maas.
sectorNotes.energy: A net consumer of grid power and process heat.
sectorNotes.jobs: The strongest local employment of the catalog, including shift work.
sectorNotes.carbon: Process heat and freight raise the area's fossil footprint.
sectorNotes.society: Odour, trucks, and a closed façade lower amenity for nearby streets.
sectorNotes.noise: Fans, shunters, and early HGV arrivals dominate the inner 250 m.

sectorNotes.wildlife: Barrier and kill risk for badger, deer, and amphibians; lighting spills into edges.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Tyre wear, salt, and metals settle in verges and gully pots.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: Unattenuated carriageway runoff is a classic path into the Maas and Jeker.
sectorNotes.energy: No generation; induced traffic burns more fuel than the old rat-run.
sectorNotes.jobs: Construction only, plus a little induced retail at junctions.
sectorNotes.carbon: New vehicle-kilometres lock in road carbon for decades.
sectorNotes.society: Faster through-trips, but severs streets and adds traffic into adjoining neighbourhoods.
sectorNotes.noise: The worst noise profile in the catalog; night lorries travel far along the valley.

sectorNotes.wildlife: Gardens can help later, but the build clears the existing edge habitat first.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Foundations and parking increase sealed area and garden-chemical use.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: Foul water is assumed on mains; surface water still pulses into local brooks.
sectorNotes.energy: A net demand node unless roofs are fully solar — this layout is not.
sectorNotes.jobs: Trades during construction and a small ongoing service economy.
sectorNotes.carbon: Embodied concrete plus household heat; better than sprawl further out.
sectorNotes.society: Homes, street life, and walking trips are the main social gain.
sectorNotes.noise: Build phase is noisy; occupied streets are milder than a highway.

sectorNotes.wildlife: Blocks fish passage and drowns margins; kingfisher and beaver lose slack-water edges.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Borrow pits and cofferdams disturb banks during construction.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: Altered flow, temperature, and sediment. This is the highest water-body stress in the set.
sectorNotes.energy: Firm renewable output when the river is up; weaker in late summer.
sectorNotes.jobs: Civil engineering peak and a small permanent operations team.
sectorNotes.carbon: Long-lived renewable energy, with methane risk if a still basin forms.
sectorNotes.society: Flood modulation and a path across the structure; recreation on the new pond is mixed.
sectorNotes.noise: Turbines are housed; construction blasting is the noisy window.

sectorNotes.wildlife: Collision and electrocution risk for heron, buzzard, and commuting geese along the Maas.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Footings and a mown wayleave; soil impact is localised.
sectorNotes.energy: Moves renewable and grid power into the city; enables other energy gains.
sectorNotes.jobs: Line crews during stringing, then inspections.
sectorNotes.carbon: Lets cleaner power reach loads; the steel itself is a small embodied cost.
sectorNotes.society: Visual clutter and a cleared strip; some residents object to nearby spans.
sectorNotes.noise: Slight corona crackle in damp weather, rarely audible at 150 m.

sectorNotes.wildlife: A large sealed box with little edge planting; lighting is the main night-time pressure.
sectorNotes.landPollution: Slab, generators, and chemical stores on a fully engineered pad.
sectorNotes.waterPollution: Cooling blowdown and high water demand stress rivers and lakes if sited beside them.
sectorNotes.energy: The largest grid drain in the catalog — a continuous megawatt-scale load.
sectorNotes.jobs: Construction plus a specialised 24/7 operations team.
sectorNotes.carbon: Unless matched to new renewables, this is a long-lived carbon sinkhole.
sectorNotes.society: Few visitors; heat-reuse to homes is not assumed in this layout.
sectorNotes.noise: CRAH fans and generators on test days; directional but persistent.
